Lane configuration for camera PHYs

Ready to give LWN a try? With a subscription to LWN, you can stay current with what is happening in the Linux and free-software community and take advantage of subscriber-only site features.
By Martin Lindqvist
September 24, 2026

Camera sensors on laptops rarely talk to the system on chip directly. Between them sits a physical-layer block, the CSI PHY, that turns the sensor's serial lanes into something the image front end can consume. How many of those lanes carry data, and in what order, is a property of the board rather than of the sensor or the chip, and that is exactly the kind of fact the kernel expects to find in the device tree.

A patch series posted in September for the camss driver fixes a case where that fact was read and then ignored. On the x1p42100, the driver set up the PHY for four lanes regardless of what the endpoint said, so a two-lane sensor probed without complaint and then produced nothing but black frames. Nothing in the logs pointed at the PHY; the sensor's own registers looked right and the pipeline reported frames arriving on time.

The fix itself is small. Rather than a table of lane masks per chip, the driver now reads the data-lanes property from the endpoint and programs only those lanes, in the order given. The larger change is in how the series tests it: each supported chip gets a check that the lane mask the driver computes matches what the device tree describes, so the next chip added cannot quietly repeat the mistake.

Why it took so long to find

Several developers had seen the black frames and blamed the sensor driver, the image signal processor, or the software ISP in libcamera. Each of those layers had its own plausible bug, and each was fixed in turn without the frames changing. It was only when someone compared the PHY registers against a vendor kernel that the lane count stood out. The comparison script is now part of the series.

csiphy0: lanes 0x1f (4 data + clock), endpoint says <1 2>
csiphy0: lanes 0x07 (2 data + clock) after the fix

The series is expected to land in the media tree for the next merge window. Distributors carrying the earlier workaround, which forced the sensor into four-lane mode, will want to drop it at the same time, since the two together leave the PHY and the sensor disagreeing again in the other direction.
